title: The Case of the Missing Bridge Stones
markdown:
The Whispering Arches Rooftop Concert was about to begin, and the air thrummed with excitement and last-minute jitters. High above the city, Corin the sable bridge runner darted back and forth, a flash of dark fur who loved to leap and twirl and end in a giggling heap. Beside him Lyra the clouded leopard tuned her gleaming violin, patterned tail twitching with the crowd’s buzz. Nearby Moss the wombat mason stacked colourful mismatched bricks for a stage decoration that looked, honestly, a little wobbly.

“One more run-through of Sunbeam Serenade,” Lyra chirped, voice warm honey. “Let’s make it shine.”

Corin bounced, ready for a dramatic spin. His leap found a stray brick. Boing. He tumbled end over end, fluffy pile, delighted laughter. Moss, brow furrowed over his tower, grunted and placed another brick with a solid thump, not looking up.

Then an enormous gust, not a breeze, a shove. Lyra shrieked as her sheet music scattered like startled birds. “Oh dear.” Paws scrambled for runaway notes.

Corin rushed to help, his own papers flying, and his sharp eyes caught the Whispering Arches looking wrong. A big section missing. A dark gap.

“Hey. What’s that?”

“The wind must have been incredibly strong,” Moss rumbled, steadying the tower, still not seeing the bridge.

They tried again. Lyra’s tinkling melody, notes like dewdrops. Corin was meant to tap. Tap, tap, tap. Then a thunderous crash from Moss’s corner. The tower went ker-plunk in a colourful cascade.

“Oh, botheration.” Moss looked sheepish. He hated it when creations would not stay put.

Picking up bricks, Lyra gasped. “Look.” Another piece gone from the Arches, the same size as the first gap.

“Two missing stones,” Corin said, fur bristling. “And that was a very strange wind. Pushy. As if something shoved it.”

“Perhaps,” Lyra whispered, a shiver, “it wasn’t wind at all.”

For the finale Corin had planned a drum solo on overturned buckets. Bum-bum-ba-BUM, rooftop-shaking. His most powerful beat, and the platform lurched. Wobble, wobble.

“Whoa.” He grabbed buckets.

Lyra clutched the violin. Moss held a railing. The shaking stopped. A small hunched shadow flitted from the Arches into the maze of alleys.

“Someone’s up to no good,” Corin declared, cheer replaced by a glint. “They’re stealing the bridge stones.”

“Why?” Lyra’s gaze followed the vanish. She always asked why.

“We have to find out,” Moss said, shoulders set, already for the stairs. “And stop them before the concert is ruined.”

They followed the peculiar trail: the shove-wind, the gaps, the unstable roof. Down the stairs that smelled of tar and last week’s rain. Corin, a dark streak, scouted the grimy brick, leaping a crate, a coiled hose, a cat that had seen everything and was not impressed. Lyra kept the violin case tight, because a clue was no excuse to scratch a good instrument. Moss measured the missing gaps in his head as he walked, already knowing the stones’ weight. An alley narrowed. A bakery breathed yeast and apology. Corin spotted the figure ducking into a tiny alcove behind the old lopsided shop.

“There.” He beckoned.

A grumpy gnome, long tangled beard to a patched hat, was piling the missing stones and muttering, “Quiet, quiet. My own little peaceful place. No noisy bothers.”

“It’s Gribble,” Lyra whispered. “He lives by the quietest park. He hates noise.”

Moss stepped forward, pragmatist. “Gribble. Why are you stealing the bridge stones?”

Gribble jumped. Hat nearly off. “Oh. You lot. Your concert is terribly loud. Music, cheering, rattles my bones. I’m building a soundproof hideaway. Blessed peace.”

Lyra winced. “We are very loud. I suppose we are. You still can’t steal the bridge. The city needs it.”

“And the concert is important to us,” Corin added. “We’ve worked so hard.”

Gribble looked at the pile, then at their faces. He sighed, gusty, shoulders slump. “I suppose I didn’t think about that. But the noise. Awful.”

“We have an idea,” Moss said, eyes lighting. “A new hideaway. Truly soundproof. I know about that. And maybe you give the stones back.”

Gribble’s beady eyes twinkled. “You’d really help me?”

They did. First they returned enough stones that the Arches could be a bridge again by dusk, because the city, unlike a concert, did not take requests. Then Moss showed Gribble a super-duper soundproof nook under the roots of an ancient oak, far from the venue: packed earth, a felt lining Moss had been saving for a quieter brick, a door that closed with a satisfied fwump. Corin, surprisingly good with heavy things when motivated, made a game of not dropping anything on his own tail. Lyra, despite delicate paws, carried and also hummed a scale so soft it was almost not music, testing the nook. Gribble, now a surprisingly helpful gnome, helped re-cement the Arches, movements precise, muttering apologies to each stone as if they had been inconvenienced.

By sunset the Whispering Arches were whole. Gribble nestled in his wonderfully quiet new home. The rooftop was ready, Moss’s decorations, reinforced, surprisingly sturdy.

The concert was a roaring success. Lanterns along the Arches, whole again, took the music and threw it kindly over the river. Lyra’s violin soared. Corin’s drumming was a heartbeat through the crowd, and when he hit the buckets this time the platform only hummed, like a well-fed animal. The decorations held. Far below, from the hideaway’s entrance, Gribble watched with a tiny satisfied smile, hat on straight. From that perfect distance the joyful music was just right: a rumour of joy, not a rattle in the bones. He tapped one returned stone in time, privately, and told no one.

Corin, after the last bow, spotted Gribble’s hat-tip in the oak-shadow and returned a smaller, quieter twirl, which is a sable’s idea of courtesy. Lyra packed the violin as if it might wake someone on purpose. Moss stacked the leftover bricks into something that, for once, did not wobble, and left them as a gift by the oak, in case a gnome ever wanted a very silent garden wall.
characters: Corin (a sable bridge runner), Lyra (a clouded leopard violinist), Moss (a wombat mason)
